# 1 Enoch Chapter 25 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Watchers

---

**1** He answered me: "That great high mountain you saw — the one whose summit looks like the throne of the Lord — that is his throne. The Holy and Great One, the Lord of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit there when he descends to visit the earth in blessing."

**2** "As for that fragrant tree — no human being may touch it until the great judgment. At that time he will execute judgment on everyone and bring all things to their final end. Then this tree will be given to the righteous and the holy."

**3** "Its fruit will be food for God's chosen people. It will be transplanted to the holy place — to the temple of the Lord, the Eternal King."

**4** "Then they will celebrate with great joy, and they will enter the holy place. The tree's fragrance will fill their very bones, and they will live out long lives on earth — lives as long as your ancestors lived. In those days not a single sorrow, plague, torment, or disaster will touch them."

**5** Then I praised the God of Glory, the Eternal King, who has prepared all these things for the righteous — who created them and promised to give them these gifts.

**6** From there I traveled to the center of the earth, where I found a blessed place full of trees with flourishing, blooming branches.

**7** There I also saw a holy mountain, and just below it on the eastern side flowed a stream that ran toward the south.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 25 is the interpretive climax of the tree-of-life vision. Michael (implied speaker) identifies the throne-mountain and explains the eschatological destiny of the fragrant tree: it will nourish the elect in an Eden-restored future. The longevity promise (v. 4) echoes the antediluvian lifespan tradition. Verses 6-7 begin the transition toward the Jerusalem/Gehenna vision.*
